en_summary: @KobeissiLetter: open source AI is undercutting Big AI margins; Anthropic's Fable 5 was over 50x more expensive per token than DeepSeek's V4 Pro, and Alibaba, Moonshot and Nvidia models compete at a fraction of the cost, pressuring prices as capex surges.
text:
Open-source AI is undercutting Big AI's margins.

Even amid the rapid scale of AI, open-source models cost far less per token, the basic unit of AI computing.

For example, Anthropic’s Fable 5 model was more than 50 times more expensive per token than DeepSeek’s V4 Pro.

Other open-source models from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and Nvidia are also competing at a fraction of the cost of leading proprietary models.

As cheaper alternatives improve, proprietary AI companies will face increasing pressure to lower prices.

This could potentially squeeze profit margins all as CapEx is surging.

Keep watching open-source AI.

US CPI inflation has now been above the Fed's 2% target for 67 consecutive months.

The last time inflation was below 2% in the US was in January 2021, amid a global economic lockdown.

Compounding inflation has become the new norm in the US.

Asset owners are the only winners.

name: Tobias Carlisle
zh_summary: @Greenbackd: the stock market is a forecasting machine pricing profits over many years, so when the outlook stops deteriorating prices can turn sharply even while conditions remain dire.
en_summary: @Greenbackd: the stock market is a forecasting machine pricing profits over many years, so when the outlook stops deteriorating prices can turn sharply even while conditions remain dire.
text:
The stock market is a forecasting machine. Prices reflect what investors collectively expect profits to be over many years, not what the economy is doing today.
When the outlook stops deteriorating, even while current conditions remain dire, prices can turn sharply higher.
The clearest evidence is the gap between the market’s low and the worst point for jobs.
In every recession since 1970, the stock market bottomed before unemployment peaked. The typical lead was about seven months. In 1990–92, the market had been recovering for nearly two years before the jobless rate topped out.

text:
Tough question. Income with crash hedging but not stocks, credit or MF? Long Treasuries are the only thing that pays you real income and tends to rally in a crash. The catch is they only work in a deflationary or growth scare like 2008. That's the plain vanilla tail hedge with income, but long bonds are terrible long duration assets to hold because they bleed in real terms most of the time. 

OTM puts are true crash insurance in any environment, but they cost you money to wait. 

Frankly, I think the idea of "safe" income in a long duration asset is a bit like turning water into wine. Lots of products claim to provide it, but there are huge trade-offs in the long run so I'd personally treat income as safe income and long duration hedgers as something different. Dividend paying consumer staples might be as close as you can get to the holy grail of equity+income (but even those are paying out of tax efficient capital). These popular distribution yield funds and all the income buffered stuff are good marketing materials, but mostly counterproductive compared to something like home grown dividend strategies....
